note: G1 v5 re-open (authorized before C038): the sealed scalar-helper control ABI used by the K-SCALAR-ADD7 kernel class. No CSR address, opcode or bit position is assigned here: addresses come only from the C017 allocator output (cn_messages.h / cn_layout.json); this file registers logical names, carrier forms, operand resolution rules and the descriptor record contract. A kernel binding supplies the per-kernel operand instance data (w5_package.contract.yaml scalar block); this ABI supplies the rules it must satisfy.

carrier.address_source: generated only: csr_allocator output; a handwritten numeric address is a protocol fault
carrier.forms_rule: the architectural write form only: rs1 carries the operand register, imm carries the operand literal
carrier.rd_rule: the read leg is discarded (rd == x0); a read result of a helper CSR is never observable
carrier.operand_source: rs1 or uimm5; never a full address and never a second register pair
carrier.other_access_rule: any access to a helper CSR outside the two forms (CSRRS/CSRRC/CSRRWI-with-rd, a load/store targeting the CSR, or any other encoding) is a protocol fault in the reference

helpers.name: mfe_submit

operand.domain_rule: 0 <= index < len(launch_descriptors); the sealed kernel binding declares the table

helpers.side_effect: submits the referenced immutable direct-move descriptor; one accepted descriptor is exactly one transaction
helpers.completion: settles only through a declared local waitable event of the same kernel (its wait_events table); the kernel observes it via WAIT, never by polling the CSR
helpers.no_address_operand: the operand names an index, never the address; an address literal is rejected, not masked

helpers.name: wait

operand.domain_rule: 0 <= index < len(wait_events); wait_events[i] is the completion event of launch_descriptors[i]; the sealed kernel binding declares the table

helpers.side_effect: park this Context's NEXT issue until the referenced slot-local event reaches a terminal state; accepted in-flight work continues (park does not flush, EVT-04)

helpers.name: signal_phase

operand.domain_rule: the operand is exactly the phase enum; any other value is OPERAND_OUT_OF_DOMAIN

helpers.side_effect: one accepted instruction is exactly one PHASE_SIGNAL message to the Group; the Tile never deduplicates or merges (a repeated signal is emitted again and judged live-duplicate at the Group, EVT-14)
helpers.at_most_once_per_task_direction: a static guarantee of the compiler and Loader (EVT-15), not a Tile gate

helpers.name: task_ret

operand.domain_rule: the operand is exactly 0; any other value is OPERAND_OUT_OF_DOMAIN

helpers.side_effect: stop new issue for this Context, wait for its local events to finish, then raise EXEC_DRAINED internally; it is the retire-chain entry, never a task-success signal
helpers.chain: RET -> EXEC_DRAINED (W2 internal notice) -> RETIRE_READY -> Group RETIRE authorization -> local reclaim -> TASK_COMPLETION

operand_rules.index_scope: slot-local to the sealed kernel; an index never crosses kernel or program instances
operand_rules.no_address: a full address as operand is HAND_WRITTEN_ADDRESS / OPERAND_OUT_OF_DOMAIN, never masked or truncated
operand_rules.immutable_tables: descriptor and event tables are sealed image state: the kernel selects an index, it may not write a table

descriptor_record.authority: the field list below is the carrier-side contract; per-kernel instance entries live in the w5 scalar block
descriptor_record.no_full_addresses: a descriptor names a binding handle and offsets; the ctx/arena/scope/binding provenance tuple is supplied by the Frame/descriptor owner at submit time, never written by the kernel

coverage.authority: the binding's scalar.coverage block (w5 package contract) enforces this per package; the ABI states the invariant so a consumer cannot weaken it silently
coverage.descriptor_use: every launch_descriptors index is the operand of exactly one mfe_submit AND exactly one wait (count and set equality; a duplicate submit is rejected)
coverage.signal_use: every declared signal_phase value is signaled exactly once
coverage.retire_use: exactly one task_ret(code=0) retires the task

faults.text: an access to a helper CSR outside CSRRW x0,csr,rs1 / CSRRWI x0,csr,imm
a helper the sealed binding does not declare cannot be called
operand value outside the helper's declared domain (index, phase enum or code)
a write to the sealed descriptor or event table
a numeric CSR address or full address literal in kernel source instead of the generated name

fault_note: these are logical contract faults of the ABI; mapping into the wire fault_code enum is an implementation detail, not assigned here

reference_kernel.instance_data_authority: protocol/w5_package.contract.yaml scalar block (consumer-side): the launch_descriptors/wait_events tables and operand values live there
